title: Gas Prices Continue to Surge in U.S., Rising 14% in a Week
partialText: Soaring oil prices suggest that more increases could be in store for American drivers. Diesel, jet fuel, and other refined products are also becoming much more expensive.

title: Russia Revels in a Sudden Reversal in Fortunes as Oil and Gas Prices Soar
partialText: President Vladimir V. Putin threatened to cut off remaining gas supplies to Europe as the Iran war drives a surge in energy costs.

title: How We Analyzed the Strike on the Iranian School
partialText: Malachy Browne of our Visual Investigations team describes what satellite imagery and other evidence tell us about who might be responsible for an airstrike on an elementary school in southern Iran. The strike killed at least 175 people, according to health officials and Iranian state media.

title: Kristi Noem Survived Many Crises. Then She Crossed a Trump Red Line.
partialText: President Trump, who values loyalty, has at times tried to distance himself from his administration’s own actions when they become politically toxic.

title: At Trump’s Summit in Miami, Bolivia Makes a Political U-turn Toward the U.S.
partialText: For the past two decades, Bolivia resisted U.S. influence. A rightward shift is reorienting the country’s president toward Washington.

title: Justice Dept. Denounces Federal Judges in Fight Against Law Firms
partialText: The Trump administration had signaled earlier this week that it was ready to abandon four executive orders seeking to punish law firms, but abruptly reversed course the next day.

title: For OpenAI and Anthropic, the Competition Is Deeply Personal
partialText: A fight over Pentagon contracts shows how the leaders of Silicon Valley’s two most important A.I. start-ups are feuding over the future of the tech industry.

title: Anthropic’s and OpenAI’s Dance With the Pentagon: What to Know
partialText: Negotiations, threats and amended contracts have left plenty of questions. Here are some answers.

title: How Candidates Are Using Winks and Posts to Seek Crypto and A.I. Cash
partialText: All across America, congressional candidates are finding creative — and critics say cynical — ways to signal support for two deep-pocketed industries, A.I. and crypto.

title: How Talarico Won Texas Democrats With Love, Luck and a Little Restraint
partialText: A carefully disciplined campaign that capitalized on viral media, months of organizing and strong outreach to Latino voters helped propel James Talarico to the center of Texas politics.

title: Ahead of Midterms, Economic Warning Signs Pile Up for Republicans
partialText: With employers cutting jobs and gas prices rising amid the war in Iran, Democrats see an opportunity to press their advantage.

title: Brandon Herrera’s YouTube Gives Democrats More Hope in West Texas Race
partialText: What had been a safe G.O.P. seat was looking more attainable for Democrats after Representative Tony Gonzales bowed out in favor of a hard-right candidate.

title: How Alberto Carvalho Became L.A.U.S.D. Superintendent Despite Scandals
partialText: Alberto Carvalho was seen as a catch for the nation’s second largest school district. Then his home and office were raided by the F.B.I.

title: There Is One Crucial Reason We’re Talking About Boots on the Ground
partialText: The U.S. and Israel have no good options to address an unavoidable problem.

title: ‘Wuthering Heights,’ MAGA Style
partialText: Kristi and Corey cavorted in the swamp as D.H.S. got bogged down.

title: Hanging Up
partialText: If decreasing dependence on our phones feels impossible, we might benefit from considering what we’d want to fill the space that they occupy.

title: At Least 6 Dead as Tornadoes Slam Michigan and Oklahoma
partialText: Tornadoes damaged buildings, cut power and injured more than a dozen people in the two states as severe weather swept across the central United States.

title: Russia Attacks Kharkiv and Kyiv in Ukraine
partialText: At least 10 people were killed when a Russian missile hit a five-story apartment building in the city of Kharkiv, and Kyiv and several other regions also came under attack.

title: Historic District Rules May Keep NoHo Parking Lot From Becoming Housing
partialText: Some residents in the Manhattan neighborhood are fighting the construction of two apartment towers, which could rise up to 19 stories on the site of a parking lot.
